case: DS1 set: any non-pending prev -> pending_deletion schedules now + grace
DS2 clear: any -> active sets the schedule to null
DS3 keep: pending_deletion -> pending_deletion emits no key (existing schedule untouched)
DS4 grace constant is exactly 30 days
DS5 purity: now is not mutated and the fresh date is exactly now + grace
DS6 rule table: pending_deletion -> suspended/banned keeps the existing date (no key)
DS7 rule table: active -> suspended leaves the column untouched (no key)
DS8 rule table: suspended -> pending_deletion and banned -> pending_deletion stamp a fresh date
DS9 rule table: suspended -> active clears the schedule to null
RT1 resume: suspended -> active with a pending date resumes pending_deletion and keeps the date
RT2 resume: banned -> active with a pending date resumes pending_deletion and keeps the date
RT3 resume: a lapsed date is still kept (the cron, not the operator, decides erasure)
RT4 support cancellation: pending_deletion -> active still clears the date
RT5 no pending date: suspended/banned -> active stays active and clears the (absent) date
RT6 non-active requests equal the pure schedule rule for every prev
RT7 missing schedule: suspended/banned -> active with undefined or empty date stays active (never pending_deletion)
